mission_03: A random variable assigns numerical values to outcomes of a random experiment. Discrete random variables have a probability mass function (PMF) that gives P(X = x) for each possible value. The expected value E[X] = sum(x * P(X=x)) is the long-run average. The variance Var(X) = E[(X - E[X])^2] = E[X^2] - (E[X])^2 measures spread. Linear transformations follow: E[aX + b] = a*E[X] + b and Var(aX + b) = a^2 * Var(X). Random variables are the bridge between abstract probability and numerical computation — every ML model treats its inputs and outputs as random variables.
